goal: Connect versioned provider envelopes to protected storage through a non-default experimental application workflow.
completed: Added a non-default application credential workflow with opaque-secret, provider-envelope, and credential-file ports.
Connected the agy 1.1.2 provider envelope adapter to protected profile storage under experimental-profile-credentials.
Added synthetic end-to-end coverage for materialization, simulated official-client rewrite, and rotated refresh capture.
The feature adds no CLI command and cannot launch agy.
Complete local gate passes with 54 tests; default release behavior is unchanged.
nextActions: Review and merge the experimental credential workflow pull request, then design the first real-client gated enrollment/exec workflow and two-account validation protocol.
decisions: Direct refresh-token injection is a viable agy 1.1.2 Linux SSH profile mechanism; the official client continues to own refresh and backend requests.
Real operator-controlled state may be inspected temporarily during authorized research, but independent OAuth enrollment remains gated by product-scope and ADR approval.
openQuestions: Does Google rotate the refresh token during long-lived use, and can agy-auth capture that update atomically per profile?
What at-rest protection should project-owned refresh credentials use?

notRun: Second independently enrolled account, real-client workflow, concurrent switching, rollback journal, and upgrade behavior were not run.

risks: The contract is reverse engineered and version-specific; refresh credentials are bearer secrets and require protected storage.
doNotRepeat: Do not copy live access tokens; the minimal refresh-token envelope is sufficient.
Do not enable production switching from single-account evidence.
